data.summary: This response reports 3 tests from 96 of 100 records; 1 of 2 inferential findings show evidence at their alpha.
sentences: This response reports 3 tests from 96 of 100 records; 1 of 2 inferential findings show evidence at their alpha.
Test 1 (TEST_T) on `score` split by `plan` finds evidence of a difference at alpha 0.05 (p = 0.004). Its effect size `cohens_d` is 0.62, medium by the convention of Cohen (1988).
Test 2 (TEST_CHISQ) on `region` split by `plan` finds no evidence of an association at alpha 0.05 (p = 0.51). Its effect size `cramers_v` is 0.08.
Test 3 (TEST_T) on `seats` split by `plan` has an undefined p-value, so no verdict is read from it.
The run read 100 records; 96 passed the filters and 0 were left out for a missing value.

follow_ups.when: the table shows an association and you want to see which cells drive it
you want to see which rows depart from the overall column mix

caveats: 2 p-values here carry no adjustment for multiple comparisons, so some may fall below alpha by chance alone; this is the concern the PULSE_ADVISORY_MANY_TESTS advisory raises.
Adding a multiplicity block (for example holm) adjusts them for multiple comparisons; then read p_adjusted beside each raw p-value.
TEST_T: Rows are independent of each other, within and across groups.
TEST_T: The two-group version uses Welch's correction, so the groups need not have equal variances.
TEST_T: The average is roughly normally distributed: safe for large groups, risky for small skewed ones.
TEST_T: The p-value is two-sided: it looks for a difference in either direction.
TEST_CHISQ: Each row is counted once and rows are independent of each other.
TEST_CHISQ: It works on raw counts, never on percentages or averages.
TEST_CHISQ: Expected counts should mostly be 5 or more (Cochran's rule: none below 1 and no more than a fifth below 5); below that the p-value is unreliable, and Pulse warns when any cell is under 5.
TEST_CHISQ: No continuity correction is applied.
